meta.count_note: Screening-grade intervention library. Every economic figure is an order-of-magnitude planning estimate intended to rank options, not to replace a vendor quotation. The UI states this on every card.

capex_bases.fixed: Absolute INR, scaled by plant size band
capex_bases.per_mwh_saved: INR per MWh of annual electricity avoided
capex_bases.per_tonne_fuel_saved: INR per tonne (or kL) of annual fuel avoided
capex_bases.per_tco2e: INR per annual tCO2e abated - screening proxy where no clean physical basis exists
capex_bases.per_tonne_material: INR per tonne of annual material substituted

meta.difficulty_scale: 1 = housekeeping, 5 = major capital project with production downtime
meta.confidence_scale: high = well-evidenced across many Indian SME deployments; medium = evidenced but site-sensitive; low = promising but thin Indian evidence base

savings_models.avoided_purchase: The plant stops buying that energy entirely. Saving = stream cost x abatement fraction.
savings_models.tariff_delta: The plant still buys the energy, at a different unit price. Saving = quantity x price differential.
savings_models.fuel_switch: One fuel replaces another on an equal-energy basis. Saving = displaced fuel cost minus replacement fuel cost, which can be negative.
savings_models.price_delta: Material substitution. Saving = tonnes switched x (old price - new price).
savings_models.none: No direct stream saving; the entire cash case is carried in opex_delta_inr.

meta.substitution_cap_note: max_substitution_pct caps the share of a material stream that can physically be switched, reflecting alloy specification, blend ratio and regulatory limits. Without it the model happily recommends switching more material than the process can accept.

interventions.name: Compressed air leak survey and repair
interventions.description: Ultrasonic leak detection across the compressed air ring main, followed by tagged repair. Typical industrial systems lose 20-30 percent of compressor output to leaks; compressed air is commonly 10-15 percent of plant electricity.
interventions.why: The cheapest tonne of carbon in almost every factory. Pays back in weeks and needs no production stoppage.
interventions.evidence: BEE SME sector energy audit findings; widely replicated across Indian industrial clusters

interventions.name: LED lighting retrofit
interventions.description: Replace fluorescent, metal halide and sodium fixtures with LED across shopfloor and yard.
interventions.why: Low risk, self-funding, and it also cuts lamp replacement labour.
interventions.evidence: EESL bulk procurement programme outcomes

interventions.name: Variable frequency drives on pumps and fans
interventions.description: Fit VFDs to centrifugal pumps, fans and blowers currently running at fixed speed with throttled flow. Affinity laws mean a 20 percent speed cut is roughly a 50 percent power cut.
interventions.why: Largest reliable electrical saving available to most process plants without changing the process itself.
interventions.evidence: BEE PAT scheme documented motor system savings

interventions.name: Premium efficiency motor replacement
interventions.description: Replace IE1/IE2 motors above 7.5 kW with IE4 or IE5 units at end of life or on failure.
interventions.why: Best done on failure rather than as a forced swap; the engine flags it as opportunistic.
interventions.evidence: IEC 60034-30-1 efficiency class deltas

interventions.name: Power factor correction and capacitor bank
interventions.description: Automatic power factor control to lift PF above the utility threshold, removing penalty and releasing transformer capacity.
interventions.why: Mostly a tariff play rather than a carbon play. The engine ranks it on cash, and is explicit that its carbon benefit is small.
interventions.evidence: State DISCOM tariff penalty structures

interventions.name: Captive rooftop solar PV
interventions.description: Behind-the-meter rooftop PV sized to daytime base load. Indian specific yield is typically 1400-1500 kWh per kWp per year.
interventions.why: The headline move for most SMEs. Ceiling is set by roof area and daytime load coincidence, not by willingness.
interventions.evidence: MNRE rooftop programme benchmark costs; typical 3.5-5 year payback at industrial tariffs
caveats: Requires shadow-free roof area of roughly 8-10 sq m per kWp
Net metering rules and capacity caps vary by state DISCOM
Benefit collapses if the plant runs mainly on night shift

interventions.name: Renewable power via open access or green tariff
interventions.description: Contract renewable electricity through open access, a group captive arrangement, or the DISCOM green tariff.
interventions.why: Near-zero capex route to a large Scope 2 cut. You still buy the electricity, so the cash case is only the tariff differential - typically a small saving, and negative in states with heavy cross-subsidy surcharge. The carbon case is the reason to do it.
interventions.evidence: State open access regulations; group captive structures under Electricity Rules
caveats: Open access is often only economic above roughly 1 MW contracted demand
Cross-subsidy surcharge and additional surcharge can erase the tariff saving
Requires a genuine RE attribute claim to be Scope 2 market-method compliant

interventions.name: Steam trap survey and condensate recovery
interventions.description: Survey and replace failed steam traps, and return hot condensate to the boiler feed tank instead of dumping it to drain.
interventions.why: A genuine closed loop: the heat and the treated water both come back. Usually under an 18 month payback.
interventions.evidence: BEE boiler system audit norms

interventions.name: Waste heat recovery on flue gas
interventions.description: Economiser or recuperator on boiler or furnace exhaust to preheat feedwater or combustion air.
interventions.why: Recovers energy the plant has already paid for and is currently sending up the stack.
interventions.evidence: BEE PAT scheme waste heat recovery case studies

interventions.name: Steam line and furnace insulation upgrade
interventions.description: Re-lag bare or degraded steam and hot fluid lines, valves and flanges; repair furnace door and wall refractory.
interventions.why: Cheap, fast, and it also fixes a real shopfloor burn hazard.
interventions.evidence: Standard insulation heat loss calculations

interventions.name: Fuel switch to agri-residue briquette
interventions.description: Convert or replace a coal or furnace oil boiler to fire agri-residue briquettes. Biogenic CO2 is reported separately from the Scope 1 total under GHG Protocol.
interventions.why: The single largest Scope 1 cut available to a thermal-heavy SME, and it turns a regional waste stream into a fuel. On current prices briquettes cost MORE per GJ than coal, so this is a genuine net cost - it is the plant's biggest decarbonisation lever and it is not free.
interventions.evidence: Widely deployed in Tamil Nadu and Punjab industrial clusters
caveats: Briquette supply and price are seasonal and regionally volatile
Higher ash handling and more frequent cleaning than furnace oil
Boiler warranty and insurance implications must be checked before conversion
Biogenic carbon must be disclosed separately, not netted silently

interventions.name: Solar thermal process water preheating
interventions.description: Evacuated tube or concentrating collectors to preheat process water below 90 degrees C, cutting boiler duty.
interventions.why: Only works for genuinely low temperature duty, which is exactly where dyeing and food plants waste the most fuel.
interventions.evidence: MNRE solar thermal programme

interventions.name: Diesel genset displacement with solar plus storage
interventions.description: Reduce genset running hours by combining rooftop PV with a modest battery to ride through short outages.
interventions.why: Diesel is the most expensive electricity in the plant. Displacing it is usually profitable before carbon is even counted.
interventions.evidence: Comparative LCOE of diesel genset versus solar plus storage in India

interventions.name: Idle load elimination and production scheduling
interventions.description: Shut compressors, exhaust fans, chillers and ovens during breaks and changeovers; consolidate short batches to cut furnace and boiler warm-up cycles.
interventions.why: Almost free, but it is a behaviour change and it decays without metering and a named owner.
interventions.evidence: Energy management system case studies under ISO 50001
caveats: Savings regress within 6-9 months unless sub-metering makes the loss visible to the shift supervisor

interventions.name: Switch to recycled aluminium feedstock
interventions.description: Substitute primary aluminium ingot with verified secondary or recycled ingot for grades where specification allows.
interventions.why: Recycled aluminium carries roughly 95 percent less embodied carbon than primary and usually costs less per tonne. It is the highest-leverage circular move in the whole library.
interventions.evidence: International Aluminium Institute recycling LCI
caveats: Alloy specification and trace element limits cap the substitutable fraction
Requires qualified supplier with consistent composition certification
Customer drawing approval may be needed for structural parts

interventions.name: Increase scrap charge in steel input
interventions.description: Shift procurement toward secondary steel produced via scrap-based induction or electric arc furnace routes.
interventions.why: Roughly a 75 percent embodied carbon reduction per tonne switched, with a modest price advantage.
interventions.evidence: worldsteel life cycle inventory, scrap versus BF-BOF route

interventions.name: Substitute rPET for virgin PET
interventions.description: Move to food-grade or industrial-grade recycled PET for the share of output where regulation and specification permit.
interventions.why: Also front-runs EPR obligations under the Plastic Waste Management Rules, which mandate recycled content targets.
interventions.evidence: Plastic Waste Management Rules recycled content schedule
caveats: Food contact applications require specific grade approval
Colour and clarity constraints limit substitutable share

interventions.name: Recycled content corrugate and packaging
interventions.description: Specify recycled content board for secondary and transit packaging, and right-size box dimensions to cut material per despatch.
interventions.why: Nearly frictionless. Recycled board is cheaper and the substitution rarely needs customer sign-off for transit packaging.
interventions.evidence: CEPI recycled grade material factors

interventions.name: Blended cement substitution
interventions.description: Replace OPC with PPC or PSC, using fly ash or slag as supplementary cementitious material where structural specification allows.
interventions.why: Turns another industry's waste stream into your input, which is industrial symbiosis in its most mature Indian form.
interventions.evidence: IS 1489 and IS 455 blended cement standards

interventions.name: Recycled cotton yarn blending
interventions.description: Blend mechanically recycled cotton into yarn for the product lines where hand feel and strength permit.
interventions.why: Cotton dominates a textile SME footprint far more than its energy bill does, so this outranks most energy projects on tonnes.
interventions.evidence: Textile Exchange recycled cotton LCA
caveats: Staple length loss caps blend ratio, commonly at 20-30 percent
Export buyers increasingly require certified recycled content, which adds audit cost but also price premium

interventions.name: In-house process scrap recovery and re-melt
interventions.description: Segregate runners, sprues, trim and rejects by grade at the machine, and reintroduce them as feedstock instead of selling as mixed scrap.
interventions.why: The tightest possible loop, entirely inside the factory gate, with no supplier qualification needed.
interventions.evidence: Standard plastics and foundry yield improvement practice
caveats: Contamination control is the whole game; mixed-grade regrind destroys the benefit
Regrind ratio is capped by part quality requirements

interventions.name: Foundry sand reclamation
interventions.description: Mechanical or thermal reclamation of used moulding sand, recovering 70-90 percent for reuse and cutting both virgin sand purchase and disposal volume.
interventions.why: Solves a disposal liability and a purchase cost at the same time. Used foundry sand disposal is increasingly regulated.
interventions.evidence: Indian foundry cluster modernisation programmes in Coimbatore and Rajkot

interventions.name: Solvent recovery and reuse
interventions.description: Fractional distillation to recover 70-90 percent of process solvent for reuse in non-critical wash steps.
interventions.why: Solvent is expensive, carbon intensive and a hazardous waste liability. Recovery attacks all three at once.
interventions.evidence: CPCB hazardous waste minimisation guidance
caveats: Recovered solvent purity must be validated for the intended step, and GMP steps usually cannot accept it
Distillation itself consumes energy, which the engine nets off

interventions.name: Dye bath reuse and closed loop water recovery
interventions.description: Reuse of exhausted dye bath liquor plus RO recovery of treated effluent, cutting both fresh water heating duty and effluent load.
interventions.why: Every litre not freshly heated is fuel not burned. In Tirupur this is already a regulatory expectation, not an option.
interventions.evidence: Tirupur zero liquid discharge cluster experience
caveats: ZLD systems carry high electrical load, which partly offsets the thermal saving
Salt build-up limits the number of reuse cycles

interventions.name: Anaerobic digestion of organic waste
interventions.description: On-site digester converting organic process waste to biogas, displacing purchased LPG or furnace oil and avoiding landfill methane.
interventions.why: Counts twice: it avoids landfill methane and it displaces a fossil fuel. Digestate has fertiliser value on top.
interventions.evidence: MNRE waste to energy programme
caveats: Needs a consistent feedstock volume and composition
Requires operator skill; neglected digesters fail within a year

interventions.name: Source segregation and recycling contract
interventions.description: Segregate at source into dry recyclable, organic and hazardous streams, and contract an authorised recycler instead of mixed landfill disposal.
interventions.why: Usually cash positive because segregated dry recyclables have resale value while mixed waste carries a disposal charge.
interventions.evidence: Solid Waste Management Rules; CPCB authorised recycler framework

interventions.name: Sell process residue as another industry feedstock
interventions.description: Route residues such as fly ash, slag, spent lime, husk or press mud to cement, brick or board manufacturers as a raw material input.
interventions.why: The purest expression of the circular carbon idea: your waste becomes someone else's input and both footprints fall.
interventions.evidence: Fly ash utilisation notification; established Indian ash-to-cement offtake markets
caveats: Requires a nearby offtaker, so viability is geographic
Material must meet the receiving industry specification consistently

interventions.name: Shift bulk inbound freight from road to rail
interventions.description: Move bulk raw material inbound legs above roughly 500 km from road to rail where a siding or terminal is reachable.
interventions.why: Rail is roughly four times better per tonne-km and usually cheaper on long bulk hauls. The blocker is lead time, not cost.
interventions.evidence: Comparative modal emission factors; Dedicated Freight Corridor capacity
caveats: Longer and less predictable transit forces higher safety stock
Needs first and last mile road legs, which claw back part of the saving

interventions.name: Outbound load consolidation and route planning
interventions.description: Consolidate part loads, raise fill factor and plan multi-drop routes rather than despatching on demand.
interventions.why: Pure logistics discipline. Cuts freight spend and emissions in the same proportion.
interventions.evidence: Standard freight fill factor improvement practice

interventions.name: Supplier radius reduction
interventions.description: Requalify high-volume, low-value inputs to suppliers within a shorter radius, cutting inbound tonne-km.
interventions.why: Real but slow, and it competes with unit price. The engine ranks it low unless freight is a large share of the footprint.
interventions.evidence: Supply chain footprint studies
caveats: Local supply often costs more per unit, which can outweigh the freight saving
Evidence base in Indian SME contexts is thin, hence low confidence
